params.intro: UTM parameters are tags appended to the end of a URL. They don't change the destination page — they only tell your measurement tools where each click came from.

items.name: utm_source
items.title: Where the click came from
items.desc: Identifies the site or app the visitor came from: instagram, whatsapp, google, newsletter.

items.name: utm_medium
items.title: The channel type
items.desc: Groups similar sources together: social, email, cpc (paid ads), bio, stories.

items.name: utm_campaign
items.title: The name of the push
items.desc: Ties every link of the same campaign together: black-friday, course-launch, june-promo.

items.name: utm_term
items.title: The keyword
items.desc: Records the search term in paid ads. Optional outside Google Ads.

items.name: utm_content
items.title: The link variation
items.desc: Tells two links pointing to the same place apart: top-button vs. footer-link.

items.q: Does UTM change the destination page?
items.a: No. UTM parameters travel in the URL, but the site opens normally. They are only read by measurement tools — like Link Charts analytics, GA4 or Meta Ads.

items.q: Do I need to fill in all five parameters?
items.a: No. In practice, utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign cover most cases. utm_term and utm_content are useful for paid ads and A/B tests.

items.q: Why shorten a link with UTM?
items.a: URLs with UTM get long — bad for an Instagram bio or WhatsApp messages. By shortening on Link Charts you share a clean link and still see each campaign's clicks in real time.

scams.sectionTitle: Most common link scams in Brazil
scams.intro: Most scams arrive through a link — on WhatsApp, by SMS or email. These are the patterns that repeat the most:

items.title: Fake WhatsApp giveaway
items.desc: "Win a freebie", "exclusive coupon" or a famous brand's anniversary. The link leads to a form that steals your data and asks you to share it with your contacts.

items.title: Bank and Pix phishing
items.desc: A message posing as your bank asking you to "update your registration" or "cancel a Pix". The page imitates the real site to capture your password and app code.

items.title: Held package at the post office
items.desc: An SMS saying a package is being held and charging a small "release fee". The payment goes straight to the scammer.

items.title: Shortened link hiding the destination
items.desc: URL shorteners are also used to mask fake pages. When in doubt, check the link here before opening — and beware of urgency: "today only", "last hours".

protectItems: Be wary of urgency and prizes you never asked for
Check the site address letter by letter before typing any password
Banks never ask for passwords, tokens or payments through a link
When in doubt, type the site address directly into the browser

disclaimer.title: Important
disclaimer.body: This check queries public threat lists and is a good first filter, but it is not a guarantee: newly created scams may not be catalogued yet. Link Charts does not store the links you check.

items.q: How do I know if a link is safe before clicking?
items.a: Paste the link into the checker above. It queries Google Safe Browsing, the same phishing and malware database used by Chrome and Firefox. If the verdict is dangerous, don't open it.

items.q: I clicked a scam link. Now what?
items.a: Don't type anything on the page and close the tab. If you entered a password or card details, change the password immediately and notify your bank. If you downloaded a file, run an antivirus scan.

items.q: Does the checker store the links I paste?
items.a: No. The link is sent only to be checked against Google Safe Browsing's database and is not stored by Link Charts.

cta.title: Safe links by default
cta.description: Every link shortened on Link Charts goes through this check automatically at creation — and you also follow clicks in free analytics.
